plain.title: CO2 hydrogenation to methanol: boiling-water-cooled multitubular reactors at 70 bar with gas recycle
plain.when: CO2 and H2 react to methanol and water, exothermic and limited by equilibrium.
plain.do: Use parallel modules of 33,000 tubes (12.5 m, 3.75 cm), Cu/ZnO/Al2O3, at 70 bar, cooled by boiling water (Campos et al. 2022), and recycle the unconverted gas.
plain.why: High pressure favours methanol; boiling water holds the tubes near isothermal.
plain.check: Single-pass CO2 conversion 28.5 % against 30.4 % at equilibrium (Campos et al. 2022, abstract).

decisions.obstacle: Methanol synthesis from CO2 is exothermic and equilibrium-limited; one pass converts little CO2.
decisions.mechanism: High pressure favours methanol; tubes cooled by boiling water hold the reactor near isothermal; the unconverted gas is recycled.
decisions.operation: Six parallel modules of 33,000 tubes (12.5 m, 3.75 cm), Cu/ZnO/Al2O3, 70 bar, boiling water on the shell.
decisions.expected_change: Single-pass CO2 conversion near equilibrium (28.5 % against 30.4 %).
alternatives: Three-step process with two intermediate condensations (53.9 % per pass; same paper)
limits: Higher pressures were left out by the authors (kinetic extrapolation, condensation in the reactor, compression cost; article p. 4).

plain.title: Release the dissolved gases in two flashes, 70 bar then 1 bar, and recycle the low-pressure CO2
plain.when: The condensate of the 70 bar loop holds dissolved CO2 and light gases.
plain.do: Flash at 30 C and 69.25 bar, let the liquid down to 1 bar and flash at 30 C again; recycle that gas to the CO2 feed less a 2 % purge (Campos et al. 2022).
plain.why: Keeps the gases out of the methanol column.
plain.check: The column feed should hold about 1.285 mol % CO2.

decisions.obstacle: The condensate of the 70 bar loop holds dissolved CO2 and light gases that must not reach the product column.
decisions.mechanism: Separate the light gases at high pressure, then release most remaining CO2 by letdown to 1 bar, and recycle it to the CO2 feed.
decisions.operation: FLASH3 at 30 C, 69.25 bar; valve to 1 bar; FLASH4 at 30 C; FLASH4 gas (less 2 %) mixed with the column's gas distillate and the CO2 feed.
decisions.expected_change: Column feed nearly free of gases (1.285 mol % CO2 in stream 28).
limits: The paper's own simulated design (Aspen Plus V10, NRTL2).

plain.title: In a methanol loop, check the CO2 dissolved at 70 bar against measured solubility: the published 18.5 mol % is not physical
plain.when: The 70 bar flash liquid of Campos et al. 2022 holds 0.1855 CO2 with K 0.955, far more than any model CHEPTA offers.
plain.do: Compare the flash liquid with measured CO2 solubility in methanol + water near the flash conditions before tuning anything toward the recycle of Campos et al. 2022; use the method that follows the data (PR + MHV1 here).
plain.why: The CO2 released at 1 bar returns to the CO2 compressor, so the recycle and the compression follow from the high-pressure solubility; a wrong published solubility makes the published recycle wrong too.
plain.check: Xia et al. 2004 at 313.75 K: about 0.018 to 0.021 at the flash's CO2 partial pressure, 0.108 under 7072 kPa of CO2; pure methanol under H2 at most 0.115, K at least 2.3 (Bezanehtak et al. 2004).
plain.result: PR + MHV1 gives 2.35 % and PR 3.41 %, against 18.545 % in Campos et al. 2022; the CO2 recycle is 394.4 against 2786 kmol/h.
